bull.b: A focused therapeutic strategy around CCL24 and fibro-inflammatory diseases gives Chemomab a defined scientific identity and development path. Concentrating resources on related indications may support platform leverage and clinical specialization if its candidates demonstrate meaningful efficacy.

Very low leverage reduces fixed financial obligations and avoids the interest burden associated with debt-funded development. This provides greater flexibility in allocating resources to clinical programs and limits balance-sheet pressure while the company remains pre-revenue.

The narrower 2025 loss and reduced cash burn indicate some expense discipline despite the absence of revenue. If maintained, this trend could extend the company’s operating runway and make available capital more productive as clinical development continues.

bear.b: The company has not yet demonstrated revenue traction, so its business model remains dependent on advancing clinical assets toward later-stage value creation. Persistent operating losses limit internal funding capacity and leave profitability contingent on successful development outcomes.

Ongoing negative operating and free cash flow means Chemomab cannot currently fund its activities from operations. Continued development therefore requires external financing, creating sensitivity to funding availability and the risk that future capital needs could constrain program execution.

Declining equity and assets show that sustained losses are consuming the company’s financial base rather than building retained resources. If this pattern continues, balance-sheet resilience may weaken further and additional financing could create value dilution or reduce strategic flexibility.
